fy_label_note: December fiscal year; Baba FY labels equal calendar years. Window per stage 4 rule: last five fiscal years (FY2021 to FY2025, actuals) plus FY2026 consensus. Within that window margins rose every year to an FY2025 peak, so the only peak-to-trough move is FY2025 actual (17.52%) to FY2026 consensus (16.94%); the trough is an estimate. Context outside the window: FY2019 was the all-time high at 22.08% and FY2020 the COVID trough at 12.17%; FY2025 is still 455 bps below FY2019, while the peer median rose 443 bps over FY2019 to FY2025 (WU, WISE, EVTC, GPN, PAYO). WISE uses a March fiscal year (Baba FY2026 = year to March 2026). Metric is VA standardized EBITDA, which reconciles to company adjusted EBITDA (FY2025 $743.7M; Weller doc 175256 says $743M).

peers.peer_note: Format [FY2025 %, FY2026E %, decline bps]. Money transfer (WU, WISE), ATM networks (NATL), card and merchant processing (EVTC, GPN), cross-border B2B payments (PAYO). RELY dropped (negative EBITDA in the window); IMXI not tracked in Baba. GPN FY2026 includes the Worldpay deal, so its decline is partly mix.

management_attribution.quote: First, U.S. immigration enforcement continued to weigh on cross-border transaction volumes, primarily from the U.S. to Mexico. This was a market-wide dynamic as the broader U.S. outbound remittance market experienced its first annual decline in more than a decade.
management_attribution.speaker: Mike Brown, Chairman and CEO

management_attribution.quote: The second-largest driver of the softness was a difficult comp to the prior year's second quarter, where we saw unusually high margins from a non-recurring fee rebate in Pakistan and certain one-time FX opportunities.
management_attribution.speaker: Mike Brown, Chairman and CEO

management_attribution.quote: Our Money Transfer results tracked the industry in the fourth quarter, reflecting the same macroeconomic and immigration-related pressures facing U.S. senders. However, while the broader market contracted on a full-year basis, our business delivered a modest increase in remittance volumes for 2025.
management_attribution.speaker: Rick Weller, CFO

prior_dated_targets.target: FY2026 EBITDA about $800M on about $4.5B revenue; adjusted EPS growth 10% to 15%
EBITDA margin +100 to 200 bps over three years

track_record.track_record_note: FY2024 adjusted EPS $8.61, 'rounding down to 15%' (Weller, doc 47507). FY2025 adjusted EPS $9.61 (Weller, doc 175256) = 11.61% growth, just under the 12% low end. FY2026 consensus EBITDA $758.5M sits about 5% below the $800M guide.

tenure.tenure_note: 10-K executive officer table via data_profile: Brown 'July 1994', 'co-founded Euronet in 1994 and has served as its chief executive officer ever since'. The stage 3 record's 'CEO since 1996' is superseded.

deciding_facts: The current dip is industry-wide: peer median EBITDA margin falls 160 bps FY2025 to FY2026E (WU -447 bps on the same US immigration shock) against 59 bps at EEFT, ratio 2.73, and EEFT's gap to the peer median narrows from -1,296 to -811 bps.

It is not clean macro: margin falls on revenue up 5.5% (FX and CoreCard), FY2025 EPS growth of 11.6% missed the 12% to 16% guide, and FY2025 margin is still 455 bps below the FY2019 peak while the peer median rose 443 bps over the same span.
